title: Few partition patterns recur across organisms regardless of classification

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Few partition patterns recur across organisms regardless of classification

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because a closed surface divided into a small number of faces admits only a small number of arrangements, the same few configurations of cells (and of parts and organs) recur in all kinds of plants and animals with no relation to biological classification.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This is the simple reason why we meet in such a case as we have been discussing (viz. the arrangement of a group or system of eight cells) with the same few types recurring again and again in all sorts of organisms, plants as well as animals, and with no relation to the lines of biological classification

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Topology of space-partitioning”. Scope: small cell groups and partitioned organs across plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The recurrence and taxonomic-independence components admit comparative tests after defining topology classes. Current datasets are taxonomically biased, and the loose quantitative wording weakens discrimination.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classify contact topologies of matched-size cell groups across taxa and test whether a small recurrent set explains most observations and whether topology is independent of classification after geometry is controlled.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Small number' and 'same few' lack fixed thresholds.

Public imaging is concentrated in model organisms and homologous stages.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A three-lineage sample of early embryos can show whether a few cell-partition types are shared. That is a fragment of a claim that also covers organs and the whole of plants and animals, most of which is uncompiled. Shared topology is only weakly discriminating once the number of legal partitions is already small.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Assemble partition topologies of small cell groups and of small organs across plants and animals, and test whether the same few graphs recur with weak phylogenetic signal. The same configurations in distant lineages, and relatedness adding little once topology is constrained, would support the claim; configurations clustering by clade would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
If only a few topologies are possible, recurrence is expected and does not by itself explain why those topologies were used.

Organs, as opposed to early cell groups, are not coded as partition graphs in these databases.
